beats.text: Look around your room.
beats.scene_description: A simple bedroom interior with white walls, a window with blue sky visible outside, a bed with a pillow, and a small desk with a lamp. A stick-figure character with a round head stands in the center of the room, looking around with a calm expression.

beats.text: The walls around you,
beats.scene_description: A close-up view of a simple room corner showing two plain walls meeting at a right angle, with a small stick-figure character on the left side of the frame looking at the wall surface.

beats.text: the light overhead,
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character standing on the ground, looking upward with head tilted back. Above their head, a simple yellow sun or light bulb shape shines down from the top of the frame, casting light on the character.

beats.text: the air going in and out of your lungs without you ever thinking about it.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character standing still with a neutral expression. Curved blue arrows flow in and out of the character's chest area to show breathing happening automatically and calmly.

beats.text: All of it feels permanent, like the world has always been like this.
beats.scene_description: A simple indoor scene showing a room with walls, a floor, a window, and furniture. A stick-figure character stands in the middle with a satisfied, confident expression, surrounded by objects that look solid and unchanging.

beats.text: It hasn't.
beats.scene_description: The same room from the previous beat, but now a large red X is drawn across the entire scene, indicating that this permanence is false or negated.

beats.text: Rewind far enough, and this exact spot becomes a place that would kill you in under a minute.
beats.scene_description: A barren, rocky alien landscape with jagged grey rocks scattered across the ground and a dark sky above. A stick-figure character stands alone in this harsh, lifeless environment, looking small and vulnerable.

beats.text: There is no air you could breathe.
beats.scene_description: The same barren rocky landscape, but now with a large red X drawn over the stick-figure character's face/head area, and a crossed-out blue air/wind symbol floating nearby to indicate no breathable air exists.

beats.text: There is no air you could breathe.
beats.scene_description: A desolate rocky plain beneath a dark empty sky, completely devoid of any air currents or atmosphere. A stick-figure character stands motionless, looking distressed, with no visible air or wind around them.

beats.text: The ground is literally liquid rock, and the sky glows orange like the inside of a furnace.
beats.scene_description: A dramatic scene showing a glowing orange sky filling the upper half of the frame like the inside of a furnace. The ground below is bright red and yellow with flowing, wavy liquid rock forming the landscape. A small stick-figure character stands on the molten ground, appearing tiny against the intense heat.

beats.text: For more than 99% of this planet's existence, nothing remotely like you was here.
beats.scene_description: A vast, empty ancient landscape with bare rocks and mountains under a hazy sky. The scene stretches far into the distance with no signs of life or humanity. On a small timeline label in the corner, '99%' is written in bold to show this huge span of time.

beats.text: For more than 99% of this planet's existence, nothing remotely like you was here.
beats.scene_description: The same ancient, lifeless landscape, but now a tiny stick-figure character appears as a small outline or ghost-like shape in the far distance, with a red X drawn over it to show that humans did not exist during this time.

beats.text: Earth got along just fine without us for four and a half billion years.
beats.scene_description: A spinning Earth planet fills most of the frame, shown in blues and greens with swirling white clouds. A timeline label reading '4.5 BILLION YEARS' appears in the corner. A small stick-figure character is positioned outside the planet, looking at it from a distance.

beats.text: Something was ruling the planet that entire time,
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric jungle or swamp landscape with tall ferns and plants. Large dinosaur silhouettes loom in the background and foreground, dominating the scene. The sky is hazy and green-tinted.

beats.text: and for almost all of it, it was nothing you'd recognize.
beats.scene_description: An underwater or alien-looking scene with strange, unrecognizable creatures—odd blob shapes, tentacled forms, and bizarre organisms—scattered across the frame against a murky background. These creatures look nothing like familiar modern animals.

beats.text: Four and a half billion years is a number your brain simply can't hold.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character standing alone, with visible stress lines or a confused expression on their face. Above their head, the number '4,500,000,000' is written in large, overwhelming font that fills much of the upper frame, towering over the character to show how incomprehensibly large it is.

beats.text: So forget the numbers for a second. Think of it like this.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character standing with a relaxed, thoughtful posture, hand raised to chin as if thinking. The large number from the previous beat is now crossed out or fading away. A simple background with open space suggests the character is clearing their mind.

beats.text: Imagine a stadium filled with popcorn.
beats.scene_description: A large sports stadium filled completely with white popcorn kernels piled high. The popcorn fills the entire interior of the stadium from floor to the top of the seating areas. A tiny stick-figure character stands at ground level for scale, appearing minuscule against the massive mound of popcorn.

beats.text: If all of that popcorn represented the entire history of Earth, then all of human history would be equal to one single kernel near the top of the pile.
beats.scene_description: The same stadium filled with popcorn, but now a single, slightly larger kernel is highlighted or circled with a red outline near the top of the pile. A label points to it reading 'ALL OF HUMAN HISTORY'. The rest of the enormous pile of popcorn represents the rest of Earth's 4.5 billion year history.

beats.text: That is how small we actually are.
beats.scene_description: A tiny stick-figure human stands alone in the center of an otherwise empty, vast landscape stretching to the horizon in all directions, emphasizing their minute scale.

beats.text: We are a single grain of sand in the whole Sahara Desert,
beats.scene_description: An enormous desert landscape with endless golden sand dunes stretching to the horizon. A single tiny grain of sand is highlighted or circled in the foreground, with a tiny stick figure next to it for scale.

beats.text: a single drop of water in the entire ocean.
beats.scene_description: A vast blue ocean filling most of the frame, with waves and horizon stretching into the distance. A single small water droplet is highlighted or circled in the foreground, with a tiny stick figure standing nearby for scale.

beats.text: So what would happen if you stepped out onto Earth as it was four and a half billion years ago?
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character stands at the edge of a barren, rocky alien landscape, looking out with uncertainty or concern toward an extreme, inhospitable scene ahead.

beats.text: Well, the first thing that happens is, you die. The entire surface is an ocean of lava under a thick orange haze of carbon dioxide.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character collapses or falls on a hellish landscape of bright red and orange lava, with thick orange fog or haze filling the sky above, creating a completely hostile environment.

beats.text: There's no moon in the sky either. It hasn't formed yet.
beats.scene_description: A dark night sky filled with stars above a barren, lava-covered alien landscape, with no moon visible anywhere in the sky.

beats.text: A planet about the size of Mars, which scientists named Theia, has just slammed into the young Earth at an angle.
beats.scene_description: A massive reddish planet labeled 'THEIA' is shown colliding with or impacting a larger planet against a starry black background, with the collision happening at an angle.

beats.text: The crash threw an enormous spray of debris into orbit,
beats.scene_description: A massive explosion of rock and debris erupts from the collision point, with fragments and dust spraying outward into space around the two colliding planets.

beats.text: and over millions of years that debris will slowly clump together into the moon you see in the sky.
beats.scene_description: A series of rocky fragments scattered in orbit around Earth gradually moving closer together and merging, eventually forming a moon-shaped sphere in the dark space above the planet.

beats.text: The same impact also knocked the planet over by about 23 degrees.
beats.scene_description: A simple diagram showing a planet with an arrow or tilt indicator showing the planet tilted at approximately 23 degrees from vertical, with labels or a degree marker visible.

beats.text: And that little tilt is the only reason we have seasons at all.
beats.scene_description: A simplified view of a tilted planet with one side facing toward a sun (labeled or positioned clearly) and the other side tilted away, illustrating how the tilt creates seasonal variation.

beats.text: Day one and a slightly different impact would have meant we never happened.
beats.scene_description: A ghost-like or faded image of a stick-figure human with a red X drawn through it, floating above the ancient Earth, suggesting that under different circumstances, humanity would not exist.

beats.text: Once the lava cooled and the first oceans formed, life appeared.
beats.scene_description: An underwater seafloor scene showing a young ocean with simple wavy water at the top, a rocky bottom, and a few tiny simple microorganism shapes scattered in the water.

beats.text: But you would not have recognized it as life at all.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure human stands looking down at a microscopic slide or magnified view showing strange, unrecognizable blob-like shapes and squiggles, with a confused or skeptical expression.

beats.text: For the next two billion years, this planet belonged to things too small to see.
beats.scene_description: A simple landscape of ancient Earth with a bright sun, blue ocean, and rocky ground, but completely empty of visible life. In one corner, a microscope or magnifying glass reveals tiny invisible microbes, emphasizing their invisibility to the naked eye.

beats.text: They were single-celled microbes, a whole living world that was invisible to the naked eye.
beats.scene_description: A close-up underwater view of a few tiny, round or rod-shaped microbes scattered across a blue-tinted background. A magnifying glass fills the left side of the frame, showing the microbes enlarged inside it.

beats.text: They were single-celled microbes, a whole living world that was invisible to the naked eye.
beats.scene_description: An ancient Earth landscape with a blue ocean, grey rocks, and a tan sky. The surface is covered entirely with tiny green and blue specks representing microbes, but they are so small they appear as a general haze rather than individual creatures.

beats.text: There were no plants, no animals, nothing with a face at all, just specks of slime running the entire Earth.
beats.scene_description: A barren ancient Earth landscape with grey and brown rocky terrain, a blue ocean in the distance, and a hazy sky. No recognizable plants, animals, or faces anywhere—just empty, lifeless-looking ground covered in microscopic life too small to see.

beats.text: There were no plants, no animals, nothing with a face at all, just specks of slime running the entire Earth.
beats.scene_description: A wide view of the entire planet Earth as a sphere floating in space against a black starry background, its surface a mix of blue oceans and grey-brown continents, all covered with invisible microscopic organisms.

beats.text: Do not mistake them for primitive.
beats.scene_description: A close-up of a few microbes with simple shapes (circles, rods, spirals) on a blue background. A small stick-figure character stands nearby with an expression of surprise or respect, pointing at the microbes.

beats.text: These specks ruled longer than every plant, every animal, and every dinosaur that ever lived combined.
beats.scene_description: A timeline or calendar representation with large text reading '3 BILLION+ YEARS' next to a swarm of tiny microbes on the left. On the right, a small cluster showing a plant, an animal, a dinosaur, and a human figure stacked together, much smaller in scale.

beats.text: These specks ruled longer than every plant, every animal, and every dinosaur that ever lived combined.
beats.scene_description: An ancient ocean floor covered with tiny microbes, filling the entire frame. In the far background, a faint transparent outline of a dinosaur and a plant appear very small and distant, showing the microbes' dominance in time.

beats.text: The air back then would have killed you.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character standing on barren ancient Earth, looking up at a hazy brown-purple sky with no oxygen. The character has an X through it or a sickly expression, showing they cannot breathe this air.

beats.text: One breath of it with no oxygen at all, and you'd drop where you stood.
beats.scene_description: A stick-figure character in the act of collapsing to the ground on barren ancient Earth, with a thought bubble or visual effect showing them gasping for air. The sky is a toxic brown-purple color with no visible oxygen.

beats.text: Then those microbes did something that almost ended everything.
beats.scene_description: A colony of microbes at the bottom of an ancient ocean, with a few of them glowing or highlighted to show they are different or beginning to do something new. A sense of change or transformation in the water above them.

beats.text: Some of them learned to eat sunlight.
beats.scene_description: A few microbes near the ocean surface reaching up toward rays of sunlight coming down from above. The sun is visible at the top of the frame, and the microbes are oriented upward, absorbing the light.

beats.text: We call it photosynthesis.
beats.scene_description: A simple diagram-style scene showing a microbe with an arrow pointing inward labeled 'sunlight' and an arrow pointing outward labeled 'oxygen'. The microbe is centered on a blue ocean background.

beats.text: Photosynthesis gives off a waste gas, oxygen.
beats.scene_description: A microbe at the bottom center of the frame releasing small bubble-like particles upward. The bubbles are labeled 'O2' or simply shown as small circles floating up through the blue water toward the surface.

beats.text: To you, oxygen is life.
beats.scene_description: A modern stick-figure human character on present-day Earth, breathing in deeply with a happy or healthy expression. Green trees and blue sky surround them, showing a world with oxygen.

beats.text: To almost everything alive back then, it was poison.
beats.scene_description: An ancient ocean scene with many microbes showing distress or death (small X marks through them, fading away, collapsing). Oxygen bubbles rise around them, causing the visible harm.

beats.text: As it built up in the air, it wiped out huge amounts of the life that couldn't handle it.
beats.scene_description: A before-and-after view of ancient Earth: on the left, a densely packed ocean floor full of microbes; on the right, the same scene mostly empty with only a few microbes remaining, while oxygen-filled air above shows the transformation.

beats.text: As it built up in the air, it wiped out huge amounts of the life that couldn't handle it.
beats.scene_description: A stark landscape of ancient Earth with scattered dead microbes (shown as small X marks or faded shapes) across barren ground and shallow water. The sky is gradually turning from brown-purple to light blue as oxygen accumulates.

beats.text: Geologists call this the Great Oxidation Event, which is a very polite name for one of the biggest die-offs the planet has ever seen.
beats.scene_description: A massive die-off scene: ancient Earth covered in the remains of countless microbes (small grey or white dots and marks everywhere), with the sky turning blue as oxygen fills it. In the corner, a text label reads 'THE GREAT OXIDATION EVENT' in bold letters.

beats.text: Geologists call this the Great Oxidation Event, which is a very polite name for one of the biggest die-offs the planet has ever seen.
beats.scene_description: A close-up view of a thin layer of ancient rock or sediment filled with fossilized microbial remains (tiny marks and shapes), representing the geological record of the extinction event. A magnifying glass or paleontologist's tools are visible at the edge.

beats.text: But the same gas did something else.
beats.scene_description: A split-screen or transitional scene: on one side, dead microbes and destruction; on the other side, oxygen molecules (shown as simple shapes or bubbles) drifting away, hinting at a new possibility or change coming.

beats.text: It stripped away the gases that had been trapping the planet's heat.
beats.scene_description: A large grey planet in space surrounded by a thick layer of colorful gases (reds, yellows, blues) swirling around it. A simple arrow or wind effect shows the gases being blown away to the right, leaving the planet increasingly exposed.

beats.text: And without them, the whole thing froze over,
beats.scene_description: The same planet now bare and grey, starting to show white patches of ice forming across its surface. The background is dark space with stars.

beats.text: very possibly from pole to pole, into a single ball of ice.
beats.scene_description: The planet is now completely covered in white ice, a featureless frozen sphere filling most of the frame against a dark starry background, with no visible land or water.

beats.text: So the air sitting in your lungs right now is the leftover from a catastrophe,
beats.scene_description: A close-up of a simple stick-figure character shown in profile, with a slightly worried expression on their face. A small transparent oval or cloud shape near their mouth represents the air in their lungs.

beats.text: one that nearly wiped out the very life that created it.
beats.scene_description: A dark underwater scene with a few tiny stick-figure organisms huddled under a thick blue-white sheet of ice above them. The ice is shown as a solid band at the top of the frame, blocking out light from above.

beats.text: Life clung on under the ice.
beats.scene_description: Beneath a thick layer of ice (shown as a white band across the top), a few microscopic organisms or simple shapes cling to rocks on the dark seafloor, barely visible but present.

beats.text: But for more than a billion years after that, the biggest thing alive was still microscopic.
beats.scene_description: A timeline or calendar strip showing '1 BILLION YEARS' in large text. Below it, a simple underwater scene with water, rocks, and a single magnified microscopic organism shown tiny against the empty space.

beats.text: Then, a little over half a billion years ago, in a burst called the Cambrian Explosion, life suddenly got big,
beats.scene_description: An underwater seafloor scene with a sudden burst of colorful, oddly-shaped creatures of various sizes—some with spikes, some round, some elongated—scattered across rocks and sand. A corner label reads '500 MILLION YEARS AGO' in simple text.

beats.text: and weird, and fast.
beats.scene_description: A close-up underwater view showing several strange creatures with unusual body shapes—tentacles, shells, segmented bodies—moving quickly across the seafloor in different directions, with bubbles or motion lines suggesting rapid activity.

beats.text: For the first time, the oceans filled with creatures you could actually see.
beats.scene_description: A wide underwater ocean scene with many visible creatures of different shapes and sizes swimming and crawling around—fish with fins, shelled animals, and other forms scattered throughout the blue water and on the sandy bottom.

beats.text: Plants crept out onto bare rock and built the first soil.
beats.scene_description: A rocky coastal landscape with a few simple green plant shapes sprouting from the grey rock and spreading outward, with brown soil beginning to form between the rocks. A simple stick figure stands in the background observing this transition from rock to green.

beats.text: Then, fish in the shallows slowly grew legs.
beats.scene_description: A shallow water scene showing the transition from sea to land: on the left, a fish with fins in the blue water; on the right, the same type of creature with stumpy leg-like appendages crawling out of the water onto wet sand.

beats.text: And the first uneasy animals hauled themselves up onto dry land.
beats.scene_description: A shoreline with a few primitive four-legged creatures (like early amphibians) awkwardly pulling themselves from the blue water up onto brown sand and rock, with looks of strain on their simple faces.

beats.text: Forests rose.
beats.scene_description: A simple landscape with several green tree shapes of varying heights sprouting upward from brown ground against a blue sky, shown in a wide aerial view.

beats.text: Swamps spread for thousands of miles.
beats.scene_description: A flat landscape filled with shallow water (blue), patches of wet mud (brown), and green plant and tree shapes spreading across the entire frame, stretching far into the distance toward the horizon.

beats.text: The coal we dig up and burn today is the buried remains of those exact forests.
beats.scene_description: A cross-section of underground showing layers of earth and rock (grey and brown), with chunks of black coal visible throughout. Above the ground surface, a simple stick figure operates a small shovel or mining tool, pointing to the coal below.

beats.text: After four billion years of fire, ice, and poison,
beats.scene_description: A split or composite view: on the left, a glowing orange planet with fire and lava; in the center, a frozen ice-covered planet; on the right, a dark planet shrouded in yellow-green toxic clouds. All three shown as small versions filling the frame.

beats.text: Earth was finally green, and warm, and alive.
beats.scene_description: A bright daytime landscape with a yellow sun in a blue sky, green trees and plants covering the land, blue water visible in the distance, and a simple stick figure standing on green grass with arms raised in a happy pose.

beats.text: And then it tried to die again.
beats.scene_description: The same green landscape with living creatures and plants, but now with dark storm clouds rolling in from the horizon, casting shadows across the land, and the sky darkening ominously.

beats.text: This is where the world gets genuinely alien.
beats.scene_description: A barren, rocky landscape under an alien-looking sky with a sun hanging overhead. Strange rock formations and sparse vegetation dot the ground. A stick figure stands in the center, looking around with a surprised expression.

beats.text: Picture Earth around 260 million years ago, long before a single dinosaur exists.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with a calendar or date stamp reading '260 MILLION YEARS AGO' in the top corner. A simple sun and sky above, with rocky terrain and low shrubs below. No dinosaurs visible anywhere on the empty landscape.

beats.text: The days are shorter here, only about 22 hours long, because the planet is spinning faster than it does today.
beats.scene_description: A side view of Earth as a sphere spinning rapidly, with curved arrows showing its fast rotation. A small clock face or '22 HOURS' label appears near the planet to show the shorter day length.

beats.text: The planet is spinning faster than it does today.
beats.scene_description: A close-up of the ground landscape rushing past quickly, with streaking motion lines showing speed. A small stick figure on the ground appears to be holding on, hair and clothes blown by wind from the fast spin.

beats.text: And the thing in charge isn't a dinosaur. Dinosaurs don't exist yet.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with rocks and plants. A large red X is drawn across a dinosaur shape that appears ghosted or faded out, showing that dinosaurs are not present in this time period.

beats.text: It's something older, and arguably worse.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with low vegetation and rocky ground under a daytime sky. A silhouette or shadow of a large predator looms over the landscape, suggesting something dangerous and alien is present.

beats.text: They were called Gorgonopsids, and they were among the very first animals on Earth to grow saber-teeth.
beats.scene_description: A rocky prehistoric landscape with a fierce Gorgonopsid creature in the center, shown as a large mammal-like predator with prominent curved saber-teeth visible in its mouth. A few rocks and low plants surround it.

beats.text: They were among the very first animals on Earth to grow saber-teeth.
beats.scene_description: A close-up view of a Gorgonopsid's head and mouth, showing the long curved fangs extending downward. The fangs are exaggerated and clearly the most striking feature of this prehistoric predator.

beats.text: The biggest of them was a monster called Inostrinsevia, which is basically the scientific name for a bear-sized killing machine,
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with a massive Inostrinsevia creature standing in the center, roughly the size of a large bear, with a muscular body and fierce predatory appearance. A tiny stick figure human stands nearby for scale, showing how enormous this creature is.

beats.text: with curved fangs as long as your hand, built to slice straight through flesh.
beats.scene_description: A close-up of the Inostrinsevia's open mouth showing enormous curved fangs, with a human hand drawn next to one fang for size comparison, emphasizing the terrifying length and sharpness of the teeth.

beats.text: built to slice straight through flesh.
beats.scene_description: A dramatic scene showing a Gorgonopsid slashing at prey with its fangs extended, movement lines and blood streaks showing the violent attack. A smaller plant-eating creature flees or falls beneath the predator.

beats.text: For a long stretch of this world, if you were a plant-eater, it didn't matter how big you grew.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape showing a large herbivorous creature (like an early mammal synapsid) grazing on vegetation. Despite its large size, it appears vulnerable and small against the vast empty landscape.

beats.text: it didn't matter how big you grew.
beats.scene_description: A size-comparison showing a very large plant-eating creature next to a human stick figure, emphasizing the creature's immense size. But the mood is tense, suggesting size alone doesn't guarantee safety.

beats.text: One of these things was waiting for you.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with a large herbivore in the distance and a Gorgonopsid predator lurking in the foreground or behind rocks, fangs visible, eyes fixed on the prey. The predator is clearly the threat.

beats.text: Strangely, the safest place to be was underwater.
beats.scene_description: An underwater scene showing the seafloor with a few small creatures and plants, calm and peaceful. Above, in the lighter waters, a few simple fish swim. No large predators are visible.

beats.text: The seas back then were calm, and mostly free of anything big enough to hurt you.
beats.scene_description: A tranquil underwater scene with gentle ripples on the surface above, a few small harmless creatures moving slowly through the water, and patches of seaweed on the seafloor. The overall mood is peaceful and safe.

beats.text: mostly free of anything big enough to hurt you.
beats.scene_description: An underwater view with a large empty open space in the water column, showing absence of dangerous predators, just a few small fish and plants scattered far apart from each other.

beats.text: On land, there were no breaks at all.
beats.scene_description: A land landscape with no rest or safety visible—Gorgonopsid predators are visible on the horizon and in the distance, multiple threats scattered across the terrain, with herbivores looking nervous or fleeing.

beats.text: And then came the closest call life on Earth has ever had.
beats.scene_description: A prehistoric landscape with the sky darkening ominously and cracks opening in the ground, suggesting something catastrophic is about to happen. A small stick figure or animal looks up nervously at the ominous sky.

beats.text: Around 252 million years ago, a region of what's now Siberia tore open and stayed open, pouring out lava across an area the size of Western Europe,
beats.scene_description: A massive landscape with the ground split open and glowing orange lava pouring out across a vast, desolate area. Flames and smoke rise into the sky. A small map or label showing 'SIBERIA' appears in a corner, with '252 MILLION YEARS AGO' marked above.

beats.text: on and off for hundreds of thousands of years.
beats.scene_description: A timeline or sequence showing the volcanic eruption continuing across a long duration—multiple frames or stages of lava flows and eruptions, with a duration label like 'HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF YEARS' to emphasize the unimaginable length of the disaster.

beats.text: It pumped so much carbon dioxide into the air
beats.scene_description: A landscape with a grey volcano on the left erupting thick plumes of smoke into the sky. The air above is filled with swirling clouds of carbon dioxide particles drawn as small circular shapes.

beats.text: that the whole planet roasted.
beats.scene_description: A wide view of Earth as a large sphere filling most of the frame, surrounded by dark space with stars. The planet's surface is bright orange-red with visible cracks and heat waves radiating outward.

beats.text: The oceans heated toward bathwater temperatures,
beats.scene_description: An underwater ocean scene with the water rendered in a lighter, warm blue color. A few simple fish shapes float in the water, and wavy heat lines rise through the water upward.

beats.text: and the oxygen in the sea crashed.
beats.scene_description: The same underwater scene, but now with several dead fish lying on the ocean floor, their shapes going grey and limp. The water is the same warm blue, with no oxygen bubbles visible.

beats.text: By the time it finally ended, the overwhelming majority of species on Earth were simply gone.
beats.scene_description: A barren landscape with a grey sky, scattered bones, and a few dried-up plant stalks. Most of the ground is empty except for these sparse remains; a small stick figure stands in the distance looking at the desolation.

beats.text: By the time it finally ended, the overwhelming majority of species on Earth were simply gone.
beats.scene_description: A simple timeline or counter showing '90 OUT OF 100 SPECIES GONE' written on a flat background, with 90 small X marks and only 10 small checkmarks to visualize the extinction percentage.

beats.text: By some estimates, as many as 9 in every 10.
beats.scene_description: A row of ten simple circular shapes representing life forms, with nine of them colored grey or crossed out and only one colored bright green, illustrating the 9-in-10 extinction ratio.

beats.text: This is the event geologists call the Great Dying.
beats.scene_description: A geological cross-section showing rock layers stacked on top of each other, with a thick dark red band cutting through the middle labeled 'THE GREAT DYING' in bold letters.

beats.text: Life did not recover in a few thousand years.
beats.scene_description: A mostly empty, barren landscape with a few scattered rocks and very sparse, struggling plant sprouts. A calendar icon in the corner shows many pages flipping or a long duration of time passing.

beats.text: It came within a hair of ending altogether,
beats.scene_description: A desolate rocky landscape with almost no life visible, just bare ground and a few scattered stones. A thin red line appears above the landscape like a thread, about to snap.

beats.text: and it stayed broken for a very long time.
beats.scene_description: A grey, lifeless landscape stretching into the distance under a cloudy sky. A timeline or duration meter shows a long extended bar, representing the lengthy broken period.

beats.text: Recovery, when it came, arrived in the strangest possible form.
beats.scene_description: A landscape transition scene showing the terrain beginning to change, with the first hints of new growth appearing—a few small green sprouts pushing through grey soil.

beats.text: Rain.
beats.scene_description: A simple dark sky with water droplets falling downward onto a flat ground below.

beats.text: Starting around 234 million years ago, the skies opened.
beats.scene_description: A landscape with a timestamp or calendar showing '234 MILLION YEARS AGO' in the corner. Dark storm clouds gather overhead and the first rain begins to fall.

beats.text: Starting around 234 million years ago, the skies opened.
beats.scene_description: Heavy rain falling from dark clouds onto a landscape below, with water beginning to pool and streams forming on the ground.

beats.text: And then they simply kept going
beats.scene_description: A landscape soaked by continuous rain, with water pooling and flooding the ground, dark storm clouds stretching across the sky.

beats.text: for about 2 million years.
beats.scene_description: A timeline strip showing '2 MILLION YEARS' written on it in bold letters, positioned above the rainy landscape to indicate the long duration of the rainfall.

beats.text: A world that had been hot and bone dry
beats.scene_description: A memory-like flashback scene of a dry, cracked desert landscape with parched earth and no water in sight, harsh sunlight beating down.

beats.text: turned into a planet of constant storms.
beats.scene_description: The same landscape transformed, now covered in water and rain, with storm clouds churning overhead and lightning in the sky.

beats.text: In that soggy, transformed landscape, a group of animals that had been minor background players
beats.scene_description: A wet, rainy landscape with water and plants. In the background, a few small dinosaur shapes are barely visible among larger animal figures in the foreground, showing dinosaurs as minor and overlooked.

beats.text: finally got their shot.
beats.scene_description: The same wet landscape, but now with dinosaur figures moved to the foreground and larger, stepping forward confidently while other animals recede into the background.

beats.text: At the start of all that rain, dinosaurs were maybe 5% of the land animals.
beats.scene_description: A simple bar chart or pie chart showing 5% filled with a dinosaur-shaped section in one color and 95% filled with other animal shapes in another color, positioned above a rainy landscape.

beats.text: By the time it stopped, they were more than 90%.
beats.scene_description: The same chart or visual representation, but now flipped to show dinosaurs taking up more than 90% of the bar or pie, with other animals reduced to a tiny sliver.

beats.text: The rain didn't just refill the rivers, it handed the entire planet over to the dinosaurs.
beats.scene_description: A landscape with rivers flowing across green terrain, with rain falling from above. In the foreground, a large dinosaur silhouette stands dominantly, representing control over the planet.

beats.text: The rain didn't just refill the rivers, it handed the entire planet over to the dinosaurs.
beats.scene_description: A wide view of a prehistoric world filled with several different dinosaur shapes scattered across a landscape with plants, water, and sky above.

beats.text: And they held onto it for more than 150 million years.
beats.scene_description: A calendar or timeline strip showing '150 MILLION YEARS' written in bold letters, with a dinosaur standing beside it on a prehistoric landscape.

beats.text: You probably know roughly how their rain ends.
beats.scene_description: A peaceful prehistoric landscape with dinosaurs and plants under a blue sky with clouds, a sense of calm before a change.

beats.text: 66 million years ago, a rock around 10 kilometers wide slammed into the Earth and rewrote the rules in a single afternoon.
beats.scene_description: A large dark asteroid or rock hurtling through space toward a blue planet below, with a timeline label reading '66 MILLION YEARS AGO' in the corner.

beats.text: 66 million years ago, a rock around 10 kilometers wide slammed into the Earth and rewrote the rules in a single afternoon.
beats.scene_description: A massive explosion erupting from the surface of the Earth, with a huge plume of fire and debris shooting upward into the atmosphere.

beats.text: The impact threw so much rock and ash into the sky that the sun effectively went out for months.
beats.scene_description: A dark sky filled with swirling ash and dust clouds blocking out the light, with the sun barely visible as a dim glow behind the thick haze.

beats.text: The impact threw so much rock and ash into the sky that the sun effectively went out for months.
beats.scene_description: A landscape almost completely dark with ash raining down, a few dinosaur silhouettes barely visible on the ground below as the world turns black.

beats.text: Plants died in the dark.
beats.scene_description: Dead, withered plants lying on dark ground under a black ash-filled sky, with no sun visible.

beats.text: Everything that ate plants starved, and everything that ate those animals starved right behind them.
beats.scene_description: A large dinosaur lying dead on the ground, representing the herbivores that starved when plants disappeared.

beats.text: Everything that ate plants starved, and everything that ate those animals starved right behind them.
beats.scene_description: A large predatory dinosaur also lying dead on dark ground, showing the carnivores that followed the herbivores into extinction.

beats.text: The giants had no chance.
beats.scene_description: A massive dinosaur skeleton or corpse on barren ground under a dark, ash-filled sky.

beats.text: But the small, furry, frightened little things that could burrow underground, waded out, and eat almost anything crawled through the wreckage and survived.
beats.scene_description: A small furry mammal creature huddled near the entrance of a burrow in the ground, with ash and debris falling around it, showing it taking shelter.

beats.text: But the small, furry, frightened little things that could burrow underground, waded out, and eat almost anything crawled through the wreckage and survived.
beats.scene_description: A small furry mammal wading through dark water or debris on a devastated landscape, picking at whatever food it can find among the ruins.

beats.text: But the small, furry, frightened little things that could burrow underground, waded out, and eat almost anything crawled through the wreckage and survived.
beats.scene_description: A small furry mammal crawling across dark, broken ground surrounded by the remains of dead plants and animals, slowly moving through the devastation.

beats.text: Those small, furry survivors were mammals. Your ancestors.
beats.scene_description: A small furry mammal standing on desolate ground, looking around at the barren landscape, with a label or caption indicating 'MAMMALS - YOUR ANCESTORS'.

beats.text: And here is the part actually worth sitting with.
beats.scene_description: A stick figure character sitting down on simple ground, looking thoughtful or contemplative, with a blank sky above.

beats.text: If that asteroid misses, the dinosaurs almost certainly keep running the show, and those little survivors stay small and forgettable forever.
beats.scene_description: A landscape showing large dinosaurs dominating a green prehistoric world, with tiny mammals barely visible in the background or hidden among vegetation, showing them remaining forever small.

beats.text: If that asteroid misses, the dinosaurs almost certainly keep running the show, and those little survivors stay small and forgettable forever.
beats.scene_description: The same prehistoric world continuing unchanged, with dinosaurs thriving and ruling, while a tiny mammal stands unnoticed at the edge of the frame, insignificant and powerless.

beats.text: That rock didn't just end a world.
beats.scene_description: A massive asteroid frozen mid-impact or just after striking Earth, showing an explosive collision with flames and debris erupting from the surface.

beats.text: It opened the only door we ever had.
beats.scene_description: A small furry mammal standing in a glowing doorway or opening of light in a dark, devastated landscape, with the future beckoning beyond it.

beats.text: The single worst day in the history of large life on Earth is the entire reason you exist.
beats.scene_description: A chaotic scene of a meteor impact or asteroid collision with Earth—a large rocky object streaking down from the dark sky toward a landscape below, with explosion and fire at the impact point. A small stick figure stands far away on the ground, looking tiny and unaware.

beats.text: Even then, we very nearly didn't make it.
beats.scene_description: A barren, ash-covered landscape with a few small stick-figure humans huddled together on the ground, looking fragile and uncertain, surrounded by emptiness and fallen debris.

beats.text: When our own species, Homo sapiens, finally appeared around 300,000 years ago, we were not the only humans alive.
beats.scene_description: A simple landscape with a few different groups of stick figures scattered across the terrain—each group slightly different in appearance or pose, representing different human species coexisting in the same world.

beats.text: we were not the only humans alive. At least four other human species were here at the very same time.
beats.scene_description: Five distinct groups of stick figures positioned in different areas of a landscape, each group labeled or visually distinct from the others—showing Homo sapiens alongside four other human species sharing the same environment.

beats.text: At least four other human species were here at the very same time.
beats.scene_description: A scene showing four different stick-figure groups, each with slightly different body shapes or features, standing on flat ground separated by some distance, representing four separate human species.

beats.text: Other kinds of people, as real as we are, sharing the same world.
beats.scene_description: A landscape with multiple stick-figure groups of different types—some taller, some shorter, some with different features—all moving or standing in the same natural environment, emphasizing their equal reality.

beats.text: Some of them had been around far longer than we had.
beats.scene_description: A simple timeline or progression showing one group of stick figures on the left labeled with an earlier date, and another group on the right labeled with a later date—visually showing that one human species existed before another.

beats.text: Today, every single one of them is gone, and we are the only kind of human left standing.
beats.scene_description: A landscape with only one group of stick figures remaining in the center, surrounded by empty space and faded or ghosted outlines of where the other groups used to be—a visual representation of all other human species gone.

beats.text: We are not the main characters of this story.
beats.scene_description: A stick figure standing on a flat landscape, looking small and uncertain, with a giant planet Earth looming in the background sky above them—emphasizing their tiny, non-central role.

beats.text: We are the survivors of the survivors of the survivors.
beats.scene_description: A stick figure standing on ground, with three faint ghosted or outlined figures stacked vertically above them in the air, showing layers of survival and ancestry reaching upward.

beats.text: So look around the room one more time.
beats.scene_description: A simple interior room with furniture (a couch, a window, a lamp), and a stick figure in the center looking around with a calm expression, examining the space.

beats.text: Everything in it is balanced on top of a stack of disasters.
beats.scene_description: The same simple room interior, but now drawn on top of a tall stack of chaotic layers below—showing eruptions, collisions, ice ages, and extinction events stacked like a precarious foundation beneath the floor.

beats.text: A frozen planet, an extinction that almost wiped the board clean, and a rock from space that erased an entire world to make room for yours.
beats.scene_description: A split scene showing three events: on the left, a blue frozen ice-covered planet; in the center, an underwater scene with creatures disappearing in dark water; on the right, a meteor striking Earth with explosion and fire.

beats.text: and a rock from space that erased an entire world to make room for yours.
beats.scene_description: A large asteroid or meteor streaking down through space toward a planet below, with explosion and bright light at impact, representing the catastrophic event that cleared the way for human existence.

beats.text: Take away any single one of those, and the air never reaches your lungs,
beats.scene_description: A stick figure standing alone on flat ground, with a faded or crossed-out image of air/breath around their face, suggesting a world where humans cannot breathe or do not exist.

beats.text: and this exact moment never happens.
beats.scene_description: The same room from earlier (couch, window, lamp, stick figure) rendered as a faint ghost or outline, barely visible—showing what would not exist if any one disaster had gone differently.

beats.text: The world before us was never a warm -up act, waiting around for humans to show up.
beats.scene_description: An ancient Earth landscape with volcanoes erupting, lava flows, simple rocks and plants, and a few prehistoric creatures, with no humans present—showing a world that existed and thrived independently for billions of years.

beats.text: It was four and a half billion years of a planet that did not need us at all, running on lava, and microbes, and monsters, and luck.
beats.scene_description: A sprawling prehistoric landscape filled with lava flows, molten rock, tiny microbes (shown as dots), large dinosaur-like monsters, and swirling storms—representing a world operating for billions of years without humans.

beats.text: We are new here.
beats.scene_description: A vast ancient landscape with old rocky terrain, sparse vegetation, and a small stick figure standing alone on the ground, looking tiny and recent against the old world around them.

beats.text: Almost impossibly new.
beats.scene_description: A close-up of a small stick figure with a surprised expression, positioned in the lower corner of the frame against a backdrop of much older, larger geological formations and weathered stone.

beats.text: And the strangest part is that you were never the point of any of it.
beats.scene_description: A wide landscape showing the Earth forming over time — ancient rocks, early life forms (simple shapes), dinosaurs in the background, and a tiny stick figure standing in the foreground, clearly not the focus of all the activity around them.

beats.text: You are simply what happened to be left standing
beats.scene_description: A desolate landscape with dust and debris settling, scattered rocks and rubble slowly falling or resting on the ground, with a single stick figure standing upright and still in the center.

beats.text: when the dust finally settled.
beats.scene_description: The same landscape now calm and quiet, with all dust settled, rocks at rest on flat ground, and the stick figure standing peacefully in a clear, still world beneath a clear sky.
